title: Russian forces take Vuhledar after Ukrainian withdrawal
body:
The Institute for the Study of War assessed that Russian forces likely captured Vuhledar in Donetsk Oblast as of 1 October 2024, after a reported Ukrainian withdrawal. Euromaidan Press reported the assessment on 2 October 2024. Geolocated footage from 30 September and 1 October showed Russian forces raising flags and moving freely in parts of the town, and Russian military bloggers claimed on 1 October that it had been seized.

A Ukrainian servicemember said that part of the force had carried out a planned withdrawal to avoid being encircled. Russian sources said they had not fully cut off Ukrainian escape routes but had inflicted unspecified losses on withdrawing troops with artillery and drones.

Russia had made at least two major offensives on Vuhledar, in October and November 2022 and in January and February 2023, both of which caused significant personnel and equipment losses. ISW considered Vuhledar not a crucial logistics hub and noted that Russian forces already controlled most of the main roads into it. It said the capture was unlikely to fundamentally alter the course of offensive operations in western Donetsk Oblast, and that the coming muddy season could hinder further mechanised assaults.
